title: Glossary
markdown:
**Abandoned mutex**: a mutex whose owning thread ended while holding it; the next wait returns `WAIT_ABANDONED`. (4.03)

**Anonymous pipe**: an unnamed one-way pipe, shared by inheritance or duplication. (2.01)

**Auto-reset event**: an event that resets itself when it releases one waiter. (4.02)

**Backoff**: waiting longer after each failure before retrying. (6.02)

**Correlation id**: a number in a request that its response carries back. (5.04)

**Deadlock**: processes or threads each waiting for something another of them holds. (4.05)

**Envelope**: the common outer structure of every message in a protocol. (5.02)

**Environment block**: a child's environment variables as `NAME=value` strings ending in zeros. (1.02)

**Event (kernel)**: a kernel object that is set or reset, used to signal. (4.02)

**Exit code**: the number a process leaves when it ends. (1.03)

**File mapping**: a kernel object that maps the same memory into several processes. (3.01)

**Framing**: marking where each message begins and ends in a byte stream. (2.03)

**Handshake**: the first exchange of a connection, agreeing on protocol and version. (5.02)

**Heartbeat**: a regular "still alive" signal from a worker. (6.02)

**Idempotent**: safe to perform twice with the same effect as once. (5.04)

**Instance (pipe)**: one connection slot of a named pipe. (2.02)

**I/O completion port**: a queue collecting completions of overlapped operations. (2.05)

**Job object**: a group of processes managed and limited together. (1.03)

**Manual-reset event**: an event that stays set until explicitly reset. (4.02)

**Message mode**: a named pipe mode where each write is one message. (2.02)

**Named pipe**: a pipe any process can open by name. (2.02)

**Overlapped I/O**: starting an operation that completes later, without blocking. (2.05)

**Pipe squatting**: creating another program's pipe name first to intercept its clients. (5.05)

**Ring buffer**: a fixed array used as a circular queue. (3.03)

**Semaphore**: a kernel object with a count, allowing up to N at once. (4.03)

**Seqlock**: a sequence counter that lets readers detect concurrent writes and retry. (3.05)

**Single-instance application**: a program whose later launches hand their work to the running copy. (6.01)

**Supervisor**: a process that starts, watches and restarts workers. (6.02)

**Tag-length-value**: a field encoding that lets readers skip unknown fields. (5.03)

**Torn read**: reading part of an old state and part of a new one. (3.05)

**UIPI**: User Interface Privilege Isolation, blocking messages to higher-integrity windows. (4.04)

**Varint**: a variable-length integer encoding using 7 bits per byte. (5.03)

**WM_COPYDATA**: the window message that copies a block of data to another process. (4.04)
